senses.definition: A store or supply.

subsenses.definition: (operations) A store of goods ready for sale; inventory.
examples: We have a stock of televisions on hand.
I checked in the back of the stockroom and found some more stock.

subsenses.definition: A supply of anything, stored until used; especially, such a supply that is ready for use.
examples: Lay in a stock of wood for the winter season.

subsenses.definition: Railroad rolling stock.
examples: The Grand Trunk Railway had just purchased a large order of stock from the American Car and Foundry Company.

subsenses.definition: (card games, in a card game) A stack of undealt cards made available to the players.
Farm or ranch animals; livestock.
examples: Good ranchers must continually keep watch over the health of their stock.

subsenses.definition: The population of a given type of animal (especially fish) available to be captured from the wild for economic use.
examples: The stocks of this fishery are recovering from overfishing, but the gains can easily reverse if our husbandry efforts lapse.

senses.definition: (finance) The capital raised by a company through the issue of shares; the total of shares held by an individual shareholder.
examples: His grandpa had bought some stock in General Electric in 1905, and he refused to sell it ever after.

subsenses.definition: The price or value of the stock of a company on the stock market.
examples: When the bad news came out, the company's stock dropped precipitously.

subsenses.definition: (especially US) A share in a company.
(figurative) The measure of how highly a person or institution is valued.
examples: After that last screw-up of mine, my stock is pretty low around here.

subsenses.definition: Any of several types of security that are similar to a stock, or marketed like one.

senses.definition: The raw material from which things are made, such as feedstock.

subsenses.definition: (cooking, uncountable, countable) Broth made from meat (originally bones) or vegetables, used as a basis for stew or soup.
examples: They make beef stock from the butchery scraps that they otherwise might not have used.

subsenses.definition: The type of paper used in printing.
examples: The books were printed on a heavier stock this year.

subsenses.definition: Ellipsis of film stock.
